title: postrank Explorer number registry
description: Validates the registry specs (numbers/spec/<part>.json, settings.json) and the two registry files (data/numbers.json written by scripts/build_numbers.mjs, data/numbers-cases.json written by R). CONTRACT 5.1-5.3. scripts/build_numbers.mjs and verification/check_numbers.mjs apply $defs/spec and $defs/numbersFile with a small built-in validator (the keywords used here only) plus the cross-field rules listed in each description.

key.description: Registry key grammar (CONTRACT 4.2). Keys read <data set>.<settings>.<quantity> (notes/storyboards part1-2.md D). Setting values use settings.<name>. The builder also rejects empty dotted segments (a..b, a trailing dot).

type.description: scalar: one finite number; vector: an array (nested arrays allowed) of numbers or null; fraction: one number displayed as an exact fraction; text: a string; na: null (for example E/N with N = 0); set: an unordered array (compared as a set).

anyOf.description: one tolerance per element of the flattened value

fn.description: an engine formatter (js/pr-core.js, engine/README.md format.ts) or a named format of js/widgets/format.js NAMED_FORMATS (formatShare, formatExpectedCount; no options)

item.description: formatTuple only: the formatter applied to each element

spread.description: pass the value array as positional arguments (formatFraction, formatRatio)

reference.description: Inside args or inputs, an object with exactly one of these keys is a reference: {"$input": name, "path"?} (a named input of the same spec), {"$setting": "settings.<name>"} (a setting value; required for the options tau, lambda and w), {"$data": "<released key>", "path"?} (data/released/<key>.json through data/released/data_contract.json, or data/precomputed/<key>.json). path is dot-separated, with array indices as numbers.

input.description: A named intermediate value shared by keys of one spec: an engine call or a released-data reference.

engineKey.description: A value computed by an engine function: fn + args, or from (a named engine-call input of the same spec, so that several keys read fields of one call). Cross-field rules: fn is an exported function of js/pr-core.js and not a formatter; fn/args and from are not combined; the value at field matches type; format is required except for text (whose display is the value) and must return a string; tolerance is required for scalar, vector, fraction and set (0 allowed) and, when an array, has one element per flattened value element; settings lists every $setting used in args (derived when omitted).

field.description: dot path into the result; omit to use the whole result

settings.description: setting name -> settings.* key (or a literal descriptor such as a family name). Every $setting in args must appear here; when omitted it is derived from the $setting references, named by each setting's own name.

same_as.description: another registry key (a spec key or a case key of data/numbers-cases.json) that holds the same quantity: the two display strings must be identical (scripts/build_numbers.mjs sameAsProblems; checked by build_numbers and check_numbers)

settingKey.description: A literal setting value (tau, cap, weights, cutoffs, interval levels, seeds). The key must start with settings. and the display string is formatSetting(value) unless format names another engine formatter; a text setting displays its value.

setting.description: what the value sets: tau, lambda, cap, w, seed, level, cutoff, prior_sd, ...

spec.description: One file per Part (numbers/spec/<part>.json) plus settings.json. Files whose name starts with _ (such as _example.json) are examples: the default build skips them.

license_scope.description: default licence scope of the file's keys

anyOf.description: engine value: function, arguments as written in the spec (references unexpanded), field, the named inputs used, and the released files read
case value written by R: the released file and the row or field it comes from

entry.description: One registry entry. Cross-field rules (checked in code): value matches type; tolerance is present for scalar, vector, fraction and numeric sets; keys are unique across numbers.json and numbers-cases.json.

owner.description: the file that owns the entry: a spec file (numbers/spec/<part>.json) or the R script that wrote it

numbersFile.description: data/numbers.json or data/numbers-cases.json: registry key -> entry, keys in code-point order.
